newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND TRIO TAKE SURREY INTO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND TRIO TAKE SURREY INTO FINAL.

text.p: England trio Alec Stewart, Graham Thorpe and Adam Hollioake carried on from where they left off against Australia to fire Surrey into the Benson and Hedges Cup final on Tuesday.
All three hit half centuries as Surrey piled up 308 for eight from their 50 overs, eventually beating Leicestershire by 130 runs at The Oval.
Kent defeated Northamptonshire by 66 runs in the other semifinal.
Stewart stroked 87 in 104 balls and Thorpe hit 79 from 80 to rescue Surrey, who made an awful start by slipping to 15 for two.
The pair added 158 in 33 overs to set up Surrey's first Benson and Hedges final appearance in 16 years.
Adam Hollioake, one of the heroes in England's 3-0 drubbing of Australia in last month's one-day series, smashed 63 in just 40 balls.
Former England seamer Martin Bicknell then made short work of Leicestershire's reply, picking up four for 41 as they were dismissed for 178 in 45.3 overs.
In Canterbury, Zimbabwe leg-spinner Paul Strang and fast bowler Dean Headley dismissed Northamptonshire for just 140 to give Kent their 11th win in 12 one-day matches this season.

Headley, who missed England's first test victory against Australia due to a back strain, destroyed Northamptonshire's top order, collecting three for 16 in 26 deliveries. Strang finished with four for 29.
Kent set Northamptonshire a target of 207, thanks largely to a 100-run fifth-wicket stand between Trevor Ward (78) and England all-rounder Mark Ealham (41).
The final will be at Lord's on July 12.
